newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: Lithuanian shares struggle, gains not seen.
newsitem.headline: Lithuanian shares struggle, gains not seen.

text.p: Lithuania's bearish market struggled on Monday and dealers said the short-term outlook was not buoyant as nervousness set in ahead of six-month results.
Official list shares eased 1.18 points to 897.34 points and group A shares lost 8.63 points to 1865.06. Central market turnover improved to a modest 215,000 litas from 172,000 litas.
Block trades turned over 894,000 litas from about two million litas on Friday.
"It's flat," said one broker. "It (the market) will stay about the same (in the short-run)."
Dealers say the market is nervous about a spate of six-month results due out in July and August and has been battered by summer-induced sluggishness.
Investors are also wary of the market, which has lost over 40 percent of its value since a speculative rally in January.
Debt is viewed as a safer bet and Lithuanian T-bill auctions are consistently oversubscribed.
Even top blue chip Hermis Bank had difficulty getting started on the central market, easing to 189.00 litas from 190.00 on tiny turnover of 3,780 litas.
Hermis made up for its lacklustre central market performance in block trading, turning over about 95,000 litas at 189.00 litas.
Rival Vilniaus Bank saw no action on the central market or in direct deals, and its tentative morning price of 240.00 litas was knocked back to its last price of 230.00.
Brokers expect Hermis Bank to stay reasonably liquid at around 190.00 litas.
